# `prefer-doctest`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: style · Profile: idiomatic · Default: off · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a test whose string name is exactly the name of a declaration at the
root of the file, which can be a doctest.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A test named with an identifier, `test parse`, is a doctest: the compiler checks
that `parse` is a declaration in scope, and generated documentation shows the
test as an example of that declaration. A string name that merely repeats the
declaration's name gets neither, and silently drifts when the declaration is
renamed.

## When it fires

It fires on a top-level test whose string name, with no escapes, is exactly the
name of a function, constant or variable declared at the root of the same file.
Tests inside nested containers are left alone, as is a rename that would
collide with another test of that name. The quick fix replaces the string with
the identifier; it is not applied by `check --fix`, since it changes the test's
qualified name (`decltest.parse` instead of `test.parse`), which test filters
may match on.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const std = @import("std");

fn double(value: u32) u32 {
    return value * 2;
}

test "double" {
    try std.testing.expectEqual(@as(u32, 4), double(2));
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Doctests>
